scope: Real loopback OpenSSH server with an isolated host key and authorized key, forwarding Docker API stdio to the existing daemon. This is transport qualification, not a remote GPU deployment.
behavior: Connection construction is lazy; SSH capacity is unavailable until a remote observer is supplied.
Repeated real SSH reads returned the independently observed Docker daemon ID.
A missing container returned confirmed absence.
Rejected client key, untrusted server key and refused connection each returned observation failure, not absence.
Uploaded and streamed back 128 KiB through SSH to an owned stopped container without changing its identity.
The empty test known-hosts file remained empty; host trust was not automatically added.

cleanup.unrelatedResources: Existing gateway, sandbox and inference resources were not changed.

limits: SDK engine transport on Unix only; Windows SSH transport is not enabled.
No managed remote YAML, remote host collector or inference tunnel.
SSH URL socket paths, embedded passwords, query options and IPv6 literals are rejected; SSH config aliases are supported.
Fresh SSH connection per request; no pooling or automatic mutation retry.
SSH stderr is suppressed; authentication and transport failures surface as observation errors.
integrationNote: Concurrent CI/cache changes were integrated after live testing; SDK transport source is identical.
